difficulty.notes: Readable (non-minified) pc_login_new.js. Anchor double_submit RSA-encrypts BOTH password and username inline (i.encrypt(j); i.encrypt(k)); password is the target field, username is a same-request decoy field encrypted by the same statement. JSEncrypt is a bundled RSA primitive (not pinned). JD nocaptcha slider is vendor noise.

task_contract.anchor_definition: double_submit: the submit handler that RSA-encrypts the password inline and posts credentials.password; not checkAccountAndPwdForLogin, getCookie, or the JSEncrypt primitive.

behavior_category.subtype: RSA (JSEncrypt) encryption of credential fields inline in the submit handler
behavior_category.recompute_check: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 uses random padding; the ciphertext is not reproducible to a fixed value.

near_categories.why_not: Only the credential fields are encrypted; the request structure is otherwise plain form fields.
The value derives from the typed password via RSA, not from device/browser signals.

evidence: The same statement RSA-encrypts both username (k) and password (j); only credentials.password is the target. The handler also assembles validCode/sig/captcha fields.

answer_match.notes: 1.json case 19 code is a contiguous snippet inside double_submit, and oracle.primary_anchor is double_submit.

question_direction.notes: The visible question asks for the complete function whose own body reads #pwd, RSA-encrypts it with the public key and assembles credentials.password; it also excludes the validation helper, cookie utility and RSA primitive, so it points to double_submit.

role_diversity.notes: 0.5 covers JSEncrypt/RSA/PKCS#1/base64 primitives; 0.2 covers validation, submit-trigger/captcha path, jQuery wrappers and login response callback; 0 covers cookie/account/QR-code decoys. The 0.7 tier is intentionally empty because the target-specific construction is inline in double_submit.
